summary: Verify pinout against schematic (SD card-detect conflict, PSRAM CS, USB host polarity)
description: The learn guide (local adafruit-fruit-jam.pdf, pp.12-30) has at least one internal conflict: SD pin listing gives GPIO34 for BOTH SD_SCK and SD_CARD_DETECT. Verify against the schematic (guide Downloads section, p.309): (1) real card-detect pin; (2) PSRAM CS pin (not stated in pinout pages); (3) USB host D+=GPIO1/D-=GPIO2 order and CH334F hub topology (2 USB-A + third port on 2x16 header); (4) GPIO11 5V-gate polarity/behavior for USB host power; (5) RP2350B silicon revision on actual hardware (guide says A2 stepping -> E9 erratum applies; note pizero shipped rev 3 where Pico-PIO-USB's E9 workaround compiles OUT - chip_version <= 2 gate - which changes hot-replug behavior, see PIZERO-11b). Known-good from guide: HSTX DVI CKn/p=12/13 D0=14/15 D1=16/17 D2=18/19; I2S DIN=24 MCLK=25 BCLK=26 WS=27 IRQ=23 RESET=22 (shared with ESP32-C6 reset); SD SPI MOSI=35 MISO=36 CS=39, SDIO extra 37/38; buttons 0/4/5; NeoPixels 32; LED 29 active-low (shared with IR); Stemma I2C0 SDA=20 SCL=21.

summary: Decision: toolchain - PlatformIO/earlephilhower (prior ports) vs bare Pico SDK
description: All three prior ports used PlatformIO + earlephilhower arduino-pico. Known costs there: build_unflags=-Os mandatory (core appends -Os after your flags, last-wins; 43b COCO-30); PICO_NO_HARDWARE is defined so __not_in_flash_func silently no-ops in C files (must use .time_critical section attrs and verify with nm - pizero hdmi-audio-notes); no LTO in shipped gcc. Pico SDK pros: pico_hdmi (HSTX+audio prior art) is SDK-based, HSTX support is first-class, LTO possible, no -Os trap; cons: lose Arduino USB host convenience wrappers (Adafruit TinyUSB), new build territory. Fruit Jam has official earlephilhower BSP support (guide p.196). Decide, then scaffold: blink + serial hello on the board. Deliverable includes deploy flow (UF2 drag or picotool).

summary: Clock plan: validate 252 MHz sys clock serving HSTX 480p + PIO-USB + emulation headroom
description: Hypothesis from research (2026-07-02): 252 MHz sys clock serves everything. Evidence: (a) PIO-USB '120/240 MHz only' was a myth - dividers derive from clk_sys, 252/48=5.25 exact in PIO 16.8 fractional divider, HW-confirmed on pizero at 252 MHz (PIZERO-44, commit 457f0ad); (b) HSTX 480p wants 25.2 MHz pixel / 252 MHz TMDS bit clock -> clk_hstx 126 MHz; pico_hdmi runs 480p at sys=126 or 252-with-div-2; (c) pizero needed vreg 1.25V at 252 (PIZERO-45) - test what Fruit Jam needs. Verify: how clk_hstx is sourced/divided when sys=252 (aux mux options: clk_sys, pll_sys, pll_usb); whether HSTX + PIO-USB + SD + emulation are all stable at 252/1.25V; measure headroom vs the ~2.4x real-time the pizero achieves. Do NOT hand-edit PLL_SYS_KHZ (breaks QSPI clkdiv - amoled lesson); use set_sys_clock_khz().

summary: HSTX DVI bring-up: 640x480p60, 320x240 RGB565 framebuffer hardware-doubled
description: First board where HSTX (hardware TMDS serializer, GPIO12-19) drives the video - no PIO bit-bang, near-zero CPU for scanout. Evaluate: fliperama86/pico_hdmi (Unlicense, v0.0.7, scanline-callback API, ~6us/callback budget, double-buffered DMA, includes audio data islands for later FRUITJAM-14) vs pico-examples dvi_out_hstx_encoder (minimal, video-only). Target: 640x480p60 CEA timing, 320x240 RGB565 internal framebuffer scanned out 2x (pizero-proven scale: CoCo 256x192 centered in 320x240 -> 512x384 on screen). Consumer model per porting-rp2350.md matrix: self-clocked scanout + SRAM budget -> static framebuffer + pointer swap, presentation on core 1. Acceptance: stable test pattern on a monitor over the DVI port at true 60 Hz.

summary: USB host keyboard behind the CH334F hub (CFG_TUH_HUB - untested in any prior port)
description: PIO-USB host on D+=GPIO1/D-=GPIO2 feeding an onboard CH334F 3-port hub (both USB-A jacks are hub ports) - so TinyUSB CFG_TUH_HUB=1 is MANDATORY and is new territory: no prior port ever enabled hub support (pizero has no CFG_TUH_HUB flag). Also: drive GPIO11 to enable host 5V. Sys clock per FRUITJAM-03 (252 MHz divides exactly for PIO-USB). Known constraints carried from pizero: USB 1.1 full-speed only (high-speed-only keyboards won't enumerate; simple wired boards + 2.4GHz dongles work); hot-replug broken on rev-3 silicon (TX SM pins D+/D- at J after enumeration, unplug shows as ~180/s flood of byte-identical HID reports; fix designed - detect N identical reports then pio_usb_host_stop/restart - but never implemented, see FRUITJAM-17); workaround = cold-boot with keyboard attached. Open question: does the always-attached CH334F hub change enumeration/replug behavior (hub stays enumerated; keyboard plugs into hub port)? That may actually IMPROVE hot-plug vs the pizero. Acceptance: HID keyboard reports arriving with keyboard on either USB-A port.

summary: microSD bring-up: SPI + FatFS, ROMs readable
description: SPI mode first (MOSI=35, MISO=36, CS=39, SCK + card-detect per FRUITJAM-01), ~12.5 MHz like pizero. Carry the lessons: cold-boot SD init is flaky - retry loop (43b: 5x, 200ms); skip macOS ._* dotfiles in the FatFS enumerator (PIZERO-10). SDIO mode (extra data pins GPIO37/38) is a stretch goal only if SPI throughput becomes a real problem (it didn't on prior ports). Acceptance: list files and read a ROM image from a FAT32 card.

summary: TLV320DAC3100 audio DAC bring-up: I2C config, I2S out, tone test
description: First target board with real audio hardware. TLV320DAC3100 configured over I2C (Stemma/I2C0 bus? verify address + bus in FRUITJAM-01/schematic), fed over I2S: DIN=24, MCLK=25 (optional - DAC PLL can run from BCLK), BCLK=26, WS=27, IRQ=23. CRITICAL sequencing: reset pin GPIO22 is SHARED with the ESP32-C6 reset - guide warns the C6 must be set up first, and toggling the shared reset clears any prior DAC setup; for the port we likely just hold C6 in a benign state and reset once before DAC config. I2S output from RP2350: PIO I2S or (if toolchain allows) HSTX is taken by video, so PIO or dedicated PIO block - plan PIO allocation across USB(1 PIO) + I2S. Outputs: 3.5mm stereo headphone + JST-SH mono speaker (class-D can add noise on headphone when both active - guide p.21). Acceptance: clean 48 kHz test tone on headphone jack and speaker.

summary: PSRAM bring-up: 8MB QMI init + usage policy (cold/bulk only)
description: 8 MB PSRAM populated (first port board with usable PSRAM; 43b had it but benched it). Init: QMI direct-mode setup (earlephilhower core has PSRAM support built in if that toolchain is chosen; else adapt 43b lib/psramlib TLSF allocator - it exists because the Pico SDK doesn't expose the needed QMI commands). POLICY per porting-rp2350.md Rule 3: PSRAM is poison in the per-frame hot path (the 43b's single biggest perf jump - 4.3x, COCO-42 - was removing a PSRAM framebuffer memcpy from an ISR). Use for cold/bulk only: ROM library cache, cassette/disk images, snapshots. CoCo RAM + framebuffers + hot code stay in SRAM. Acceptance: memtest passes over 8MB; policy documented in repo.
resolution: DONE - on-hardware memtest PASS over all 8 MB (address-in-address + 0x00/0xFF/0x55/0xAA walking patterns, pmalloc heap OK). Used the earlephilhower core's built-in QMI PSRAM support (auto-detect + memory-map; no hand-rolled init like the 43b psramlib). CRITICAL: psram_reinit_timing(clk_sys) after set_sys_clock_khz(252MHz) or high addresses read corrupt (AMOLED lesson). Measured throughput ~9.9 MB/s write / ~25 MB/s read (~10-25x slower than SRAM) - the basis for the cold/bulk-only policy. src/psram/psram_test.cpp + [env:psram]; docs/psram-policy.md documents Rule 3 (PSRAM = ROM cache / cassette-disk images / snapshots; CoCo RAM + framebuffers + hot code stay in SRAM). PSRAM currently unused (0 bytes) until a consumer (FRUITJAM-19) needs it.

summary: Vendor XRoar 1.11 core (fresh extraction from upstream, not from prior port repos)
description: Extract the emulation core from upstream ~/github/xroar at the 1.11 release tag - deliberately NOT copying the drifted coco_machine/core copies in the three port repos (they diverged from each other; user directive: prior ports are insight, not source). Scope: mc6809, mc6883 (SAM), mc6821 (PIA), mc6847 (VDG), events, minimal portalib subset (rely on -ffunction-sections + --gc-sections instead of hand-stripping - amoled AMOLED-40 lesson). Apply the two universal unlocks from day one: (1) HOT_FUNC section attrs (hot.h pattern) on the dispatch/SAM/PIA/VDG hot set - ~20% (don't spray wider, there's a knee - AMOLED-31); (2) -DSUPPRESS_RENDER_SCANLINE no-oping per-scanline render while KEEPING HS/FS timing events (BASIC's IRQ timer needs them), frame-batched palette-LUT renderer instead (~2x - COCO-47/AMOLED-57). Beware bool-macro/delegate_void_bool token-pasting hazard (why pico.h can't enter portalib). Document provenance: PROVENANCE.md + THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md per pizero convention. Acceptance: core compiles for RP2350 and passes a headless smoke test (execute N 6809 cycles of Color BASIC ROM).

summary: Boot Color BASIC: machine glue, ROMs from SD, indexed frame to HSTX display, frame pacing
description: The integration milestone: CoCo 1/2 machine config wired to the vendored core (FRUITJAM-09), ROMs loaded from SD (FRUITJAM-06), VDG frame-batched renderer producing an indexed/palette frame handed to the HSTX consumer (FRUITJAM-04). The handoff contract per porting-rp2350.md Rule 4: core produces indexed frame + vsync/dirty signal; platform consumes per its hardware. Frame pacing per Rule 5: 15000 6809 cycles per 16762us frame (~0.895 MHz authentic), deadline spin with resync-not-debt on overrun, emulation rate decoupled from the 60 Hz display. Keep CoCo RAM in SRAM (XIP cache pollution - COCO-41). Acceptance: green screen, (C) TANDY / OK prompt at authentic speed.

summary: Dual-core split: core 0 emulation, core 1 presentation
description: Follow the proven pattern (pizero/amoled): core 0 = pure emulation; core 1 = display scanout callbacks + (later) audio island/I2S feed + SD service. HSTX scanout itself is near-zero CPU (hardware serializer + DMA), so core 1 has more headroom here than on any prior board. Handoff: RP2350 SRAM is cache-coherent across cores - volatile front-buffer pointer swap (pizero) or dirty flag (amoled), no mutexes. Decide after FRUITJAM-04 chooses the scanout library (pico_hdmi's scanline callback runs on whichever core calls video init - verify). Acceptance: emulation timing unaffected by display activity; measured headroom documented.
resolution: DONE - decision recorded in docs/dual-core.md; acceptance measured on hardware. Split: core 0 = emulation + frame compose + audio resample/I2S feed + USB host + pacing; core 1 = pico_hdmi video engine only (near-zero CPU: HSTX hw serializer + DMA + per-scanline pointer callback). Deviation from the brief: audio I2S feed and SD service run on CORE 0, not core 1 - video_output_core1_run() is a non-returning while(1) loop, so core 1 can't host a service loop; the I2S DMA ring is fed non-blocking from core 0 (FRUITJAM-13). Handoff is lock-free (RP2350 SRAM cache-coherent across cores): g_fb framebuffer (single buffer, direct pointer read), g_want_resync flag. Presentation-buffering decision: SINGLE buffer, tearing accepted - two 320x240 RGB565 buffers = 300 KB don't fit (RAM ~74%, ~136 KB free); CoCo text screen is mostly static so tearing rarely visible. Measured: core 0 ~12.9ms/16.76ms field (1.29x, ~23% headroom), core 1 59-60 fps steady, no observed coupling - emulation timing unaffected by display activity. Caveat documented: cold-boot after the psram memtest env (shared QMI timing).

summary: USB HID keyboard to CoCo keyboard matrix mapping
description: Map TinyUSB HID boot-protocol reports to the CoCo PIA0 keyboard matrix in the vendored core. Port the MAPPING KNOWLEDGE from pizero (which keys go where, shift/ctrl handling, rollover behavior, BREAK=Escape etc.) but implement fresh against our core (user directive: no code copying). Includes key-repeat policy and a safe panic/reset chord. Depends: FRUITJAM-05 (reports arriving), FRUITJAM-10 (running machine). Acceptance: type a BASIC program on a real keyboard; all CoCo keys reachable.

summary: CoCo audio to the TLV320 DAC: PIA tap, 48 kHz ring, I2S sink
description: The audio seam, first-class on this board. Source side (pattern proven on pizero, implement fresh): tap PIA1 port A 6-bit DAC + single-bit sound (single-bit source is PIA1 CB2, not PB1 - pizero correction), event-driven integrate-and-dump resampler keyed to CPU cycle timestamps, emit 48 kHz mono into a power-of-two SPSC ring (pizero needed 8192 deep, primed to half, to survive fast-forward - PIZERO-39); hold-last on underrun. Sink side: core 1 feeds the ring to I2S/TLV320 (FRUITJAM-07) - a far simpler consumer than pizero's HDMI islands, no per-scanline metering, just steady I2S DMA. Note upstream-xroar issue 11 (bare-metal audio seam design) - this port is its first real I2S instantiation; feed findings back. Known open quality item: pizero's residual source-side fidelity gap vs desktop XRoar (PIZERO-41, open) - watch whether our fresh tap reproduces it. Acceptance: BASIC SOUND/PLAY commands audibly correct on headphones + speaker.
resolution: DONE - user-confirmed on hardware: Color BASIC SOUND is audibly correct out the 3.5mm headphone jack to an external amp. Deviations from the brief: (1) single-bit sound is PIA1 PB1, NOT CB2 - the issue's 'CB2' note was wrong; upstream XRoar 1.11 (vendored core) wires CB2 = sound-mux ENABLE, PB1 = single-bit. We follow the vendored source (covers both). (2) Sink runs on CORE 0, not core 1: core 1 is fully occupied by the pico_hdmi video engine, so the I2S library's own DMA ring IS the buffer (2048 frames, hold-last top-up to half), fed non-blocking once per field. (3) Resampler bug fixed: the first version shared one accumulator between the PIA hooks (fire mid-field) and render_audio (runs after the field), collapsing a whole field of DAC toggles into one clipped sample -> buzzy 60Hz spike train; replaced with an event-log resampler (hooks record (cycle,bus) changes, render replays them per sample). (4) DMA IRQ conflict fixed: earlephilhower I2S adds a SHARED handler on DMA_IRQ_0, pico_hdmi uses an EXCLUSIVE handler on DMA_IRQ_0 (core 1) that ticks the scanout state machine on every IRQ -> I2S completions desynced video (black screen); moved pico_hdmi to DMA_IRQ_1 (SPI-SD polled, PIO-USB no DMA IRQ, so IRQ_1 free). (5) faithful sound.c bus model + one-pole DC blocker R=0.9995 + AUDIO_GAIN=32000. (6) internal speaker off by default (SPEAKER_OUTPUT=0), headphone->amp; TLV320 headset auto-mute-on-insert tried but its impedance-based detector doesn't see a line/amp cable as a plug, so reverted. PLAY is Extended-only (bas12.rom is plain Color BASIC) - out of scope. Follow-ups: real-time dropped ~1.5x->1.26x from audio tap hooks in flash (HOT_FUNC candidate, FRUITJAM-15); mount_sd() hangs forever on a loose/unresponsive card instead of timing out; jack-detect auto-mute is a research item. STABILITY CONFIRMED 2026-07-06: the cross-core HSTX resync fix (commit db47ea3) held through a multi-hour BASIC-program run with no crash — the freeze is resolved.

summary: Optional: HDMI audio via HSTX data islands (second audio sink)
description: Stretch goal after FRUITJAM-13 works. Sound over the DVI/HDMI cable using data islands on the HSTX path. Prior art: pico_hdmi has TERC4 data-island audio built in (48 kHz stereo, lock-free packet queue) - if FRUITJAM-04 adopts pico_hdmi this may be nearly free; pizero's dvi_data_island.c encoder (Takano pico_lib, MIT) is the portable packet layer if we need our own (its libdvi DMA-repoint injection layer does NOT carry to HSTX). Sink caveats from pizero: some monitors ignore ACR (pitch rides the video clock); 'DVI' sinks may not do audio at all - which is exactly why the DAC (FRUITJAM-13) is the primary path. Acceptance: audio over the HDMI cable on at least one monitor, selectable vs/alongside DAC output. [2026-08-18] Promoted low->medium: user wants to explore HSTX data-island audio soon. Not urgent - the TLV320 DAC path (FRUITJAM-13) is working well - so this is a SECOND sink alongside the DAC, not a replacement; keep the DAC as the default output and make HDMI audio selectable. [2026-08-18 core-cost investigation, settled - do not re-litigate] Q: does the pico_hdmi path cost us a CPU? A: the core was ALREADY spent at FRUITJAM-04 bring-up; HSTX audio costs no ADDITIONAL core. Evidence: video_output_core1_run() (lib/pico_hdmi/src/video_output_rt.c:1378) is a while(1) that never returns, launched via multicore_launch_core1(core1_video_entry) at src/coco/coco_main.cpp:564. Core 1 is therefore unavailable for an Arduino-style service loop - which is exactly why FRUITJAM-13 deviation (2) put the I2S sink on core 0 - but it is not BUSY: docs/dual-core.md measures core 1 as 'near-zero CPU; hardware DMA', 59-60 fps steady, more idle headroom than any prior port. The constrained core is core 0: ~12.9 ms of the 16.762 ms field, ~1.29x real-time, ~23% headroom (perf-log.md: ~16% worst case seen under SOUND). WHERE THE COST LANDS: (a) core 1 scanline ISR gains hstx_di_queue_tick() + hstx_di_queue_get_audio_packet() per scanline - it already services that ISR and has the headroom; (b) core 0 encodes TERC4 packets and calls hstx_di_queue_push() - lock-free producer/ISR-consumer queue (lib/pico_hdmi/include/pico_hdmi/hstx_data_island_queue.h), no locks, but it is the 23%-headroom side and the side that grows. TWO RISKS TO DESIGN AROUND: (1) core 0 is the FRUITJAM-35-sensitive core - that freeze was core 0 blocking on a full TinyUSB CDC FIFO; hstx_di_queue_push() returning false on a full queue MUST be a sample drop, never a spin/retry. Watch hstx_di_queue_silence_count as the starvation signal. (2) DMA IRQ allocation is already delicate: FRUITJAM-13 deviation (4) found earlephilhower I2S installs a SHARED handler on DMA_IRQ_0 while pico_hdmi installs an EXCLUSIVE one, so pico_hdmi was moved to DMA_IRQ_1; re-verify that interaction when BOTH sinks are enabled at once. API already present in-tree (no vendoring needed): hstx_packet_set_audio_infoframe / set_audio_samples[_cs] (hstx_packet.h), pico_hdmi_set_audio_sample_rate(), and a DVI-mode flag that disables all data islands (video_output.h:184-187). [2026-08-26 CONSTRAINT from FRUITJAM-37 - read before starting; supersedes an earlier note on this issue that was based on a wrong root cause] The dev monitor will NOT sync to HDMI data islands: with islands enabled the coco firmware showed NO picture at all, while the same cable/input carried the DVI-mode test pattern perfectly. coco_main.cpp now defaults to COCO_DVI_MODE=1, which disables all data islands. HDMI audio REQUIRES data islands, so on THIS sink enabling FRUITJAM-14 trades away the picture entirely - the two cannot coexist here. What this does NOT mean: the precomposed compose ring is fine and still used in the HDMI path (COCO_DVI_MODE=0); DVI mode simply never touches it, because the ring exists only to carry audio islands. So FRUITJAM-14's design is intact - what changed is that it is SINK-DEPENDENT. Acceptance now requires (a) a second monitor that tolerates data islands, since the dev monitor cannot validate this feature at all, and (b) making the mode runtime-selectable rather than a build flag, defaulting to DVI/DAC, so enabling HDMI audio can never silently cost a user their display. The TLV320 DAC stays primary. [2026-08-26 the constraint note above is WEAKER than stated - read this too] The premise that this monitor rejects data islands is not established; the user reports it works with islands on other projects (see FRUITJAM-37's correction). So FRUITJAM-14 may NOT be blocked on a second sink at all. The open question is whether the blank screen came from our HDMI mode emitting audio infoframes + ACR for audio that is never configured or sent - which is precisely what FRUITJAM-14 would FIX by configuring audio properly. Run FRUITJAM-37's decisive experiment (COCO_DVI_MODE=0 + pico_hdmi_set_audio_sample_rate()) BEFORE assuming this feature is sink-limited; it may be the cheapest first step of the feature itself rather than a blocker to it. Keep the runtime-selectable + DAC-primary design points regardless. [2026-08-26 EXPERIMENT RUN - result: the malformed-audio hypothesis is DEAD; this sink dislikes well-formed islands. Supersedes the two notes above; do not re-run this.] The proposed probe (call pico_hdmi_set_audio_sample_rate() and see if the picture returns) turned out to be a NO-OP before it was even run: video_output_rt.c:319 defaults current_sample_rate to 48000 and configure_audio_packets(current_sample_rate) runs at init (line 1295). 48 kHz is also exactly this port's I2S rate, so the ACR N/CTS were never garbage and the setter would have changed nothing. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RUN: rebuilt with COCO_DVI_MODE=0 and instrumented the HDMI path with its three public counters. Result over 25 s: stale=0 (the compose ring builds immediately and NEVER falls back to vactive_di_null - no malformed active lines), lib_resync=0 (pico_hdmi's own resync counter never moves), silence ~12068/s (every island slot carrying well-formed silence packets, as expected when nothing pushes samples), 59-60 fps steady, our own desync watchdog silent. By the library's own accounting the HDMI stream is HEALTHY. ON-SCREEN, SAME BUILD: heavy horizontal lines and intermittent blanking. Note this is a PARTIAL lock, not the clean no-picture originally reported - the sink is latching and then losing it, which is a more precise symptom than we had before. CONCLUSION: nothing is wrong with what we transmit; this monitor genuinely mishandles our data islands. The original constraint therefore stands - but now measured rather than assumed, and the assumption is what got walked back twice. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR FRUITJAM-14: still viable, still sink-dependent, and it CANNOT be validated on the dev monitor - acceptance needs a second sink. Keep runtime-selectable, default off, DAC primary: on a sink like this one, enabling HDMI audio costs the user their picture, so it must never be the default or a build-time-only choice. UNTRIED ANGLES if someone wants to push further: send islands with NO audio infoframe (islands present but audio not advertised) to separate 'islands' from 'audio signalling'; or vary island placement/rate. Both are FRUITJAM-14 work, not prerequisites to it. The [di] stale/silence/lib_resync probe now lives in coco_main.cpp's periodic report and will answer this again on any sink.

summary: Performance: lock 100% real-time with headroom; keep a perf log
description: Target: authentic real-time CoCo (~0.895 MHz 6809) locked, with measured headroom for audio+USB. The playbook says the architecture (not the clock) does the work: HOT_FUNC hot set in SRAM (+20%), CoCo RAM in SRAM, frame-batched render (~2x), PSRAM out of hot path, then clock headroom last. Known non-wins to NOT chase (all measured flat on amoled): hand-devirtualizing mem_cycle without inlining (AMOLED-56), manual portalib stripping (AMOLED-40), spraying HOT_FUNC beyond the core set (AMOLED-31). HSTX should make this the easiest board yet: display scanout ~0 CPU vs 43b's ISR streaming or pizero's libdvi TMDS. Keep docs/perf-log.md from first boot (43b convention - its 11%->99.9%-locked trajectory was the most useful porting record). Acceptance: sustained 100% real-time with headroom numbers documented.
resolution: DONE - user-confirmed. Real-time is locked with headroom on the 252 MHz/1.25V operating point: idle ~12.7 ms of the 16762 us field budget (~1.3x), 59-60 fps, no desync over multi-minute runs; worst case seen was SOUND at ~14.4 ms (1.16x) pre-hot-set. Key change: the vendored core was entirely in flash - moved mc6809_run (~15 KB opcode dispatch, the biggest lever), mc6821_read/write, and the PIA sound-tap hooks + snd_compute into .time_critical SRAM via HOT_FUNC (coco_mem_cycle/VDG/renderer were already hot). Kept to the core set (AMOLED-31 knee); skipped known non-wins (AMOLED-56/40). RAM 70.9->74.0%. Clock headroom left untouched (last lever). docs/perf-log.md added with the hot-set table, numbers, methodology and open items. Open/soft: idle is a noisy benchmark (+-3%) that understates the dispatch-in-SRAM win; a fixed CPU-bound benchmark for a cleaner headline number is noted but not built.

summary: Board UI: buttons + NeoPixels
description: Button 1 = GPIO0 (also BOOT at power-on - avoid overloading in ways that trap users in bootloader), Button 2 = GPIO4, Button 3 = GPIO5. Candidate functions: machine reset, cassette/disk picker, display/audio toggles. 5 NeoPixels on GPIO32 as status (power/SD/USB/emulation-health); red LED GPIO29 is ACTIVE-LOW and shared with the IR receiver - probably leave it alone. Low priority polish; design after the milestone boots.

summary: USB hot-replug: implement the detect-and-restart fix
description: Implement the fix DESIGNED on pizero but never built (PIZERO-11b, diagnosis commit 4d47ae5): on rev-3 silicon the PIO-USB TX SM pins D+/D- at J after enumeration, so unplug is electrically invisible and manifests as a ~180/s flood of byte-identical HID reports. Fix: in tuh_hid_report_received_cb, detect >=N consecutive byte-identical reports, then pio_usb_host_stop()/restart to force re-enumeration. IMPORTANT twist on this board: the CH334F hub is always attached - the hub may absorb/report port changes properly, making replug just work (or fail differently). Test hub behavior FIRST (part of FRUITJAM-05 acceptance notes) before assuming pizero's failure mode. If we build it, offer the fix back to the pizero repo.

summary: Joystick via USB HID gamepad
description: Map a USB HID gamepad (via the hub) to CoCo analog joystick axes + fire button (PIA/SAM sampling in the core). Open on every prior port (PIZERO-13 never done) - this board could be the first to land it; the two USB-A ports make keyboard+gamepad simultaneously practical (hub permitting, USB 1.1 gamepads only). Depends: FRUITJAM-05/10/12. [2026-08-19 scope decided - generic PS3-style USB pad] Target device: user's generic PS3-style USB controller. MAPPING (agreed): left stick -> RIGHT CoCo joystick (the port nearly all software reads); D-pad -> same axes, OVERRIDING the stick when pressed, snapped to 0/32/63; right stick -> LEFT CoCo joystick; face button 0 (plus one mirror) -> right fire (PIA0 PA0); another face button -> left fire (PIA0 PA1). Both CoCo ports are in scope: the mux decode is one switch on PIA0 CB2:CA2 covering all four analog channels, so the second joystick is nearly free. THREE WORK ITEMS: (1) HID side - src/coco/coco_main.cpp:390 tuh_hid_report_received_cb currently drops every non-keyboard report (filters HID_ITF_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD); accept gamepad reports and decode axes/buttons into a shared state struct. summary: CoCo 1/2 machine glue: memory map + SAM + PIA + VDG-sync IRQ (headless boot)
description: Hand-write the CoCo machine that wires the vendored chips (mc6809 CPU, mc6883 SAM, mc6821 PIA0/PIA1, ram, ROM) - machine.c/dragon.c was deliberately NOT vendored (FRUITJAM-09), so this is the machine we own. Memory map: 32K RAM $0000-$7FFF, Color BASIC ROM (bas12.rom, 8K) at $A000-$BFFF, PIA I/O $FF00-$FF5F, SAM control regs $FFC0-$FFDF, reset/vector page from ROM. Route the CPU mem_cycle delegate through SAM decode -> RAM/ROM/PIA. Wire PIA0 (keyboard matrix - return no-key so the scan loop idles; HS/FS sync inputs on CA1/CB1) and PIA1 (VDG mode bits on PB, 6-bit DAC + single-bit sound on PA/CB2, cassette) with the minimal delegates needed to not hang. Drive CPU IRQ from PIA0's interrupt output, fed by VDG horizontal/field-sync events (keep these events live even with per-scanline render suppressed). Keep CoCo RAM in SRAM (COCO-41). Follow the upstream tag-1.11 wiring faithfully (dragon.c). Acceptance (headless, serial-verified): CPU resets to the ROM vector and executes Color BASIC into its keyboard-poll idle loop; PC sits in the poll region and the 60 Hz IRQ is ticking (visible via an IRQ counter / expected screen-RAM init to $60 spaces).

summary: Frame pacing: authentic ~0.895 MHz run loop, resync-not-debt, decoupled from 60 Hz display
description: The emulation timing loop per porting-rp2350.md Rule 5: run 15000 6809 cycles per 16762 us NTSC frame (~0.895 MHz authentic), deadline-spin to the frame boundary, and RESYNC (not accumulate debt) on overrun so a slow frame can't spiral. Emulation rate is decoupled from the 60 Hz display refresh (display consumes latest frame independently). Builds on FRUITJAM-22's machine. Depends on the SAM MPU-rate handling for cycle counting. Acceptance (headless, serial-verified): sustained real-time rate measured at ~1.0x (0.895 MHz) with the pacing loop; overrun injection shows resync (no runaway debt); report measured headroom (cycles/frame budget vs consumed).

summary: Disk (.dsk): WD2797 FDC + Disk BASIC ROM cartridge + .dsk parsing
description: Phase 2 of FRUITJAM-19 (user chose cassette-then-disk). Much larger than cassette: emulate the WD2797/WD279x floppy disk controller (a whole chip - status/track/sector/data regs, read/write/seek commands, DRQ/INTRQ), map the Disk BASIC ROM (disk11.rom) as a cartridge at $C000, wire the cartridge control register ($FF40 - drive select, motor, density, halt-enable) + NMI/HALT from the FDC, and parse .dsk images (JVC/VDK first; DMK stretch). ROMs from SD. PSRAM holds the disk image (FRUITJAM-08). Depends on FRUITJAM-28's SD/PSRAM plumbing. Acceptance: DIR a .dsk, LOAD+RUN a program off it. Consider vendoring upstream wd279x.c vs fresh - decide at start.
plan: DECISION: fresh sector-level FDC, NOT vendoring the upstream 4-layer byte-timed stack (wd279x 1152L + vdrive + vdisk + rsdos + cart/vdrive_interface) - too coupled; a JVC .dsk is raw sectors so we can serve whole sectors instead of emulating rotation/IDAM/gap timing. FOUNDATION DONE (this commit): cart ROM window $C000-$DFFF (coco_machine_load_cart), WD2797 register decode at $FF48-4B + DSKREG $FF40 in coco_mem_cycle (guarded by g_cart_rom so no-cart boots are unaffected - verified 1.30x/60fps unchanged), status reports NOT READY (0x80) so Disk BASIC boots to prompt but disk ops fail cleanly. coco_main loads 0:/coco/roms/disk11.rom into SRAM (cart executes at $C000 = hot path, not PSRAM). REMAINING (the big part): (1) FDC command engine - restore/seek/step-in/out/read-sector/write-sector/read-address state machine; (2) the CoCo HALT-based transfer - DSKREG b7 enables HALT, FDC releases the halted CPU per byte via signal_halt(halt_en && !DRQ), INTRQ->NMI on done (wire cpu->halt + MC6809 NMI); (3) JVC .dsk parse (256B*18sec*35trk*1side raw) from SD into PSRAM, track/sector -> offset; (4) write-back / write-protect. GATED ON TESTING: needs a 16 KB Ext+Color main ROM (bas.rom) + disk11.rom + a .dsk on the SD card - none available to me, so the FDC engine is best built against real ROMs+image next session.
resolution: DONE - user-confirmed on hardware: DIR lists a JVC .dsk directory and LOADM loads+runs a machine-language program off it. Fresh sector-level WD2797 FDC (not the vendored 4-layer byte-timed stack): Type I Restore/Seek/Step update track+ TRACK0 status; Read/Write Sector serve whole 256B sectors from the mounted image via the CoCo HALT-based transfer (halt = halt_enable && !DRQ; each byte sets DRQ + releases the halted CPU, the $FF4B access clears DRQ + re-halts + schedules the next byte; last byte -> INTRQ->NMI, halt auto-clears). DSKREG $FF40 + WD2797 $FF48-4F decode guarded by g_cart_rom (no-cart boots unchanged). coco_machine_mount_dsk parses JVC geometry. coco_main assembles 16K Ext+Color from extbas11+bas12 and maps disk11.rom at $C000. Stable over a multi-hour BASIC run. FOLLOW-UPS: sector writes (SAVE) modify the PSRAM copy only, not persisted back to SD (write-back to the card is a TODO); no on-screen disk/file picker yet (natural fit for FRUITJAM-16 buttons); Read Address/Read Track/Write Track (format) not implemented (not needed for DIR/LOAD/RUN).

summary: Virtual cassette AUDIO playback: hear a .wav/.aiff tape through the sound mux (MOTOR/AUDIO ON)
description: Play/hear real audio files as if they were a cassette in the deck - distinct from FRUITJAM-28 (which decodes the .cas FSK bitstream into PIA1 PA0 for CLOAD data). Here the tape's ANALOG level is routed to the sound output so you actually hear it: on a real CoCo, MOTOR ON (PIA1 CA2 relay) spins the deck and AUDIO ON selects the cassette as the sound-mux source, sending tape audio through the TV/DAC. Mechanism is already half-present in the vendored core: sound.c has a 5-source audio multiplexer with SOURCE_TAPE (sound.c:113) fed by snd->tape_level / the get_tape_audio delegate (sound.c:402-417); when the CoCo sound-mux select bits (PIA CB2 enable + source select, same path FRUITJAM-13 tapped) pick SOURCE_TAPE, that level mixes to the 48kHz ring -> TLV320. So the port work is: (1) a fresh minimal .wav (PCM 8/16-bit mono/stereo->mono) + .aiff loader from SD into PSRAM (FRUITJAM-08 policy - images are cold/bulk); (2) a sample feeder clocked at the CoCo tape rate (resample the file's rate to the tape playback timebase, reusing the event system like FRUITJAM-28's .cas feeder) that writes the current analog level into tape_level, GATED by the MOTOR relay (CA2) so MOTOR OFF pauses playback; (3) wire the sound-mux SOURCE_TAPE path so AUDIO ON is audible (verify the CB2/select decode reaches sound.c mux_source). Shares the SD+PSRAM+motor plumbing with FRUITJAM-28; can share one 'virtual cassette' abstraction that carries either a .cas (data) or .wav/.aiff (audio) payload. Acceptance: insert a .wav/.aiff via the deck, MOTOR ON + AUDIO ON, and hear the file play through headphone/speaker; MOTOR OFF pauses, AUDIO OFF silences it. Stretch: also hear the FSK tones of a .cas during CLOAD (same tape_level path). OUT OF SCOPE, decided 2026-08-26: this port is not doing audio-based tape loading. summary: Lockup: KALEIDSC freezes the board after running for a while
description: Reported 2026-07-07: the KALEIDSC (kaleidoscope) program locks up the board after running for some time - screen frozen, no input, requires power-cycle (to confirm). This is a NEW freeze, distinct from the one closed in FRUITJAM-13's resolution (the cross-core HSTX resync fix, commit db47ea3, which held through a multi-hour plain-BASIC run) - so either that fix doesn't cover this path or this is a different fault. KALEIDSC is graphics-heavy (hi-res PMODE + likely SOUND/PLAY), so suspects to investigate: (1) VDG mode the renderer doesn't fully handle - KALEIDSC uses PMODE hi-res graphics, and FRUITJAM-24's frame-batched renderer was built/accepted for text+semigraphics first; an unhandled/edge graphics mode or a bad SAM video-address wrap could read out of bounds or spin. (2) audio ring / resampler edge under sustained SOUND/PLAY (FRUITJAM-13 event-log resampler) - overflow or a cross-core stall. (3) the same cross-core HSTX resync class of bug (db47ea3) recurring under a different load, or DMA_IRQ_1 (pico_hdmi) vs I2S DMA_IRQ_0 interaction. (4) a slow real-time overrun spiral if KALEIDSC pushes >100% (FRUITJAM-23 was supposed to resync-not-debt - verify it actually holds here). (5) memory: stack/heap corruption or a wild pointer that only manifests after N minutes. NEEDS DIAGNOSIS before a fix: reproduce, capture whether serial is still alive when frozen (core 0 vs core 1 dead), get PC/state if possible. REPORTED DETAILS (2026-07-07): loaded from a .dsk via LOADM (so the disk/Ext+Color build, FRUITJAM-29 path); froze after ~1 hour of running; serial-alive-at-freeze not yet known; reproduction in progress. First diagnostic priority = is serial still printing after the screen locks (core 0 alive => display/core-1 fault; serial dead => core-0 hang/hard-fault); the loop prints an 'emu N fields ... fps ...' line every 60 fields (coco_main.cpp:602) so a frozen-but-alive core 0 will keep emitting these. RULED OUT (2026-07-07, code-checked): (a) the frame-pacing deadline spin (coco_main.cpp:592) uses rollover-safe int32 math ((int32_t)(deadline-micros())), so the ~71-min micros() 2^32-us wrap is NOT the cause via the main pacing loop. (b) SAM double-speed: KALEIDSC (a Forth program, source at ~/github/coco/src/kaleidoscope/kaleidoscope.fs) toggles the SAM speed bit $FFD7/$FFD6 every field, but coco_machine.cpp:38 states fast-cycle rate is NOT modelled - the writes are decoded (line 618, handed to sam->mem_cycle) but don't change cycle counting, so no crash path there. (c) KALEIDSC is SILENT (semigraphics-4 video only, no SOUND/PLAY/single-bit), so the audio ring/resampler is almost certainly not involved - the ring just holds-last silence. (d) the program's writes are all in-bounds $0400-$05FF (sg4-addr math verified), so it is not corrupting itself. LEADING SUSPECT now = display/core-1 path (same class as the db47ea3 cross-core HSTX resync fix / DMA_IRQ_1): screen froze under continuous vsync-locked heavy core-0 load; a rare cross-core race or DMA hiccup could wedge core 1 while core 0 runs on. DECISIVE TEST outstanding = serial-alive-at-freeze (core 0 keeps printing 'emu N fields' => core-1/display fault; silent => core-0 fault). NOTE: first capture attempt (2026-07-07) produced no log - the pio device monitor was not actually running/streaming; must confirm the monitor is live before the next repro. CAPTURE RUN (2026-07-07, scripts/serial_logger.py self-reconnecting timestamped logger -> kaleidsc-freeze.log): NEGATIVE REPRO - KALEIDSC ran ~2h40m (16:51->19:33) rock-steady at 1.04x real-time / 59-60 fps, field counter to 607500, NO freeze; then a clean 2-sec USB re-enumeration + fresh boot banner (reset-button/power-cycle, NOT a hang). KEY FINDINGS: (1) This DISPROVES all deterministic ~1hr timer-wrap theories - the run sailed past both the micros() 72-min 2^32-us wrap and the audio cycle-counter ~80-min wrap with zero disturbance. So the freeze is intermittent/probabilistic OR depends on a condition absent this time. (2) KALEIDSC is the TIGHTEST load tested: ~1.04x real-time (16045 of 16762 us/field, ~4% headroom) vs 1.28-1.34x for idle BASIC - its SAM-double-speed compute loop pins the emulator near the frame budget for hours. Steady/flat, no leak. (3) LEADING HYPOTHESIS: the only difference vs the freezing runs is the serial monitor was ATTACHED (host continuously draining the USB CDC) this whole run. Build uses -DUSE_TINYUSB so Serial = Adafruit TinyUSB CDC, whose write() can BLOCK core 0 in a flush loop when the TX FIFO fills and no host reads it; loop() does an unguarded Serial.printf every field (coco_main.cpp:602). If true, attaching a monitor MASKS the freeze (host drains FIFO) - fits 'freezes in normal use, fine with monitor'. CAVEAT: unproven - if the CDC drops writes when disconnected (DTR low) instead of blocking, the correlation is coincidence and the freeze is just rare. NEXT STEPS (proposed): (a) DEFENSIVE FIX regardless of cause: guard the per-field Serial.printf so it can never block (only print if Serial/CDC connected & writable, or make non-blocking) - removes a variable and fixes it outright if CDC-block is the cause. (b) DIAGNOSE WITHOUT SERIAL: add independent per-core heartbeat LEDs/NeoPixel (FRUITJAM-16) - core-0 and core-1 each toggle their own indicator so the next normal (no-monitor) freeze shows on the board itself which core died, decoupling diagnosis from the masking variable. (c) re-repro without monitor to reconfirm timing. IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-07, both fix+heartbeats, builds clean -e coco, RAM 75.9%): (1) DEFENSIVE FIX - guarded every per-field Serial write in loop() with `if (Serial && Serial.availableForWrite() >= N)` (coco_main.cpp) so a connected-but-not-draining or absent USB CDC host can never block core 0 in a full-TX-FIFO write; the fps/desync-watchdog LOGIC still runs unconditionally, only the printf is dropped when the FIFO is full. (2) HEARTBEAT - core 0 toggles the onboard LED (PIN_LED=29, active-low) from loop() with rate encoding core-1 health read from video_frame_count: slow ~2Hz blink = both cores alive, fast ~8Hz = core 0 alive but core 1/video stalled, FROZEN LED = core 0 hung. This diagnoses the next freeze on the board itself with no serial host (the masking variable). AWAITING: user flashes firmware.uf2, runs KALEIDSC without a monitor for a long session. Outcomes: no freeze => Serial-block was the cause (fixed); frozen LED => core 0 still hangs elsewhere; fast-blink-frozen => core 1/display fault. STILL a bug until user-confirmed stable over a long no-monitor run. Do NOT mark done until root-caused and the fix is user-confirmed stable over a long run.
resolution: DONE - user-confirmed on hardware (2026-07-09): with the fix (commit 6e8bea2) flashed, KALEIDSC - the exact reproducer - ran continuously for >24 hours with NO freeze, vs the ~1-hour lockups before. ROOT CAUSE: an unguarded per-field Serial.printf in loop() (coco_main.cpp) could block core 0 in a full-TX-FIFO write. Build uses -DUSE_TINYUSB so Serial is the Adafruit TinyUSB CDC; when no host drains the CDC (normal use, no serial monitor) the TX FIFO fills and the write stalls core 0 -> hard freeze needing a power-cycle. KALEIDSC triggered it (vs plain BASIC) because its SAM-double-speed compute loop pins the emulator near the frame budget (~1.04x real-time, ~4% headroom) with the tightest sustained core-0 load tested. The bug was MASKED whenever a serial monitor was attached (host drains the FIFO) - which is exactly why the 2h40m capture run on 2026-07-07 never reproduced it and mis-pointed at the display/core-1 path. FIX: guard every per-field Serial write with `if (Serial && Serial.availableForWrite() >= N)` so an absent/stalled CDC host can never block core 0 (fps/desync-watchdog logic still runs; only the printf is dropped when the FIFO is full). Also added a per-core heartbeat on the onboard LED (GPIO29) - it stayed on the slow ~2Hz both-cores-alive blink throughout, so it wasn't needed for this diagnosis but remains as on-board instrumentation for any future no-serial freeze. Key lesson: an unguarded Serial.print in a tight main loop is a latent core-0 hang on TinyUSB CDC whenever no host reads it - audit other ports for the same pattern.

summary: Audit prior RP2350 ports for the same unguarded Serial.print core-0 hang (FRUITJAM-35 class)
description: FRUITJAM-35 root cause: an unguarded per-field Serial.printf in loop() blocks core 0 when the TinyUSB CDC TX FIFO fills and no host drains it (normal use, no serial monitor) -> hard freeze needing a power-cycle. This is a GENERIC TinyUSB-CDC hazard, not Fruit-Jam-specific: any tight main loop that prints every frame/field without checking availableForWrite() is a latent core-0 hang whenever nothing reads serial. The masking is nasty - it only bites in normal use and disappears the moment you attach a monitor to debug it. Audit the three prior Waveshare RP2350 ports (43b / pizero / amoled) and any shared code for per-loop Serial.print/printf without a `Serial && Serial.availableForWrite() >= N` (or equivalent connected+space) guard; apply the same guard where found. The Fruit Jam fix pattern is in coco_main.cpp (commit 6e8bea2). Deliverable: each prior port checked, guards added where the pattern exists, and a note back in their issue trackers referencing FRUITJAM-35. Cross-repo so it lives here as the originating find.

summary: No picture in coco firmware: monitor will not sync to HDMI data islands
description: SYMPTOM: the coco firmware showed NOTHING on the monitor while every serial boot stage was clean - SD mounted, ROM loaded, disk cart mounted, video init ok, clk_sys=252/clk_hstx=126 MHz, core 1 holding 59-60 fps with no desync warnings. The emulator was running correctly the whole time; only the picture was missing. ISOLATION: env:display (the FRUITJAM-04 HSTX test pattern) displayed perfectly on the SAME cable, connector and input, proving the physical path and the 640x480p60 mode were fine. ROOT CAUSE: display_test.cpp runs DVI mode (no data islands); coco_main.cpp ran HDMI mode (data islands on). pico_hdmi's own header warns 'Some monitors have trouble syncing with HDMI Data Islands' (video_output.h:184-187). This monitor is one of them. The islands were carrying nothing useful anyway - this port's audio goes out the TLV320 I2S DAC. FIX (COCO_DVI_MODE build flag, default 1) - and note it took THREE attempts, the first two of which were committed or flashed while broken: (1) WRONG: set_dvi_mode(true) while leaving the precomposed/native path AND the 320-wide video_output_init(). In DVI mode the active line is the static vactive_line_dvi list, whose last word is HSTX_CMD_TMDS | rt_h_active_pixels; initialised at 320 it emits a HALF-LENGTH line against a 320-halfword DMA the expander doubles to 640. Result: link desyncs at ~160 fps continuously. This is what commit 2512104 shipped. (2) WRONG: DVI mode + the classic 320-word copy scanline callback. Correct picture, but the per-line copy on core 1 (~9.2M word-accesses/s) contends with core-0 emulation for SRAM and starves the HSTX FIFO - ~6-second sync-loss bursts every 1-2 minutes, self-recovering, 8 resyncs in 210 reports. This reintroduced exactly the underrun the native pointer path had been adopted to eliminate (see the comment on scanline_ptr_cb). (3) CORRECT (under test): video_output_init at the FULL 640x480 OUTPUT size + set_dvi_mode(true) + native_pixel_mode + the scanline POINTER callback, and NO compose ring. The ring is only needed to carry audio islands, and DVI mode never consults it, so the low-cost pointer handoff is available without data islands. The command list and the DMA now agree on 640. MEASURED (attempt 3): 1 desync in 318 reports over ~5.3 min, self-recovered, vs 8 resyncs in 210 for attempt 2 and continuous desync for attempt 1. PROCESS LESSON: the failure mode is a burst every 1-2 minutes, so a 15-25s capture CANNOT see it - and I twice declared success off exactly such a capture. Any video-path change here needs a multi-minute soak counting desyncs, not a boot log. A clean serial log proves the RP2350 is TRANSMITTING, never that the sink is DISPLAYING. OPEN BEFORE THIS CAN BE CALLED DONE: (a) the 10-minute soak must finish clean and be confirmed on-screen by the user; (b) commit 2512104 is known-bad and must be corrected in history; (c) that residual single desync is unexplained - if it recurs, it is the real remainder and gets its own issue rather than holding this one open. SEE ALSO: FRUITJAM-14 (constraint note - HDMI audio is sink-dependent), FRUITJAM-38 (core-0 timing step, found during this soak, NOT caused by this change). [2026-08-26 ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED - the earlier text above overstates it] The claim 'this monitor will not sync to HDMI data islands' is NOT supported: the user reports the same monitor handles data islands fine on other projects. One observation (islands on = no picture) was generalised into a property of the hardware. The evidence only supports the narrower claim: THIS FIRMWARE's HDMI-mode output is not displayed by this monitor. LIKELIER MECHANISM, untested: coco_main.cpp never configures HDMI audio - no pico_hdmi_set_audio_sample_rate(), not one sample pushed - yet HDMI mode unconditionally emits audio infoframes and ACR packets every 4th blanking line (video_output_rt.c:736, 935-943), with N/CTS derived from a sample rate that was never set. The stream advertises and clocks audio that does not exist. A sink can accept well-formed islands and still reject that. DECISIVE EXPERIMENT (not yet run): build COCO_DVI_MODE=0 and call pico_hdmi_set_audio_sample_rate() with a real rate before starting video. Picture returns -> confirms malformed audio signalling and REOPENS HDMI mode as viable. Still blank -> the island hypothesis survives in some form and needs a different probe. Either way the shipped fix stands on its own merit: this port sends no HDMI audio, so DVI mode costs nothing today and is the correct default until something needs islands. [2026-08-26 DONE - confirmed on hardware] 10-minute soak: 589 reports, 1 desync (a single 116 fps sample that self-recovered), 588 clean at 59-60 fps; user confirmed the picture held on the monitor for the full run. Shipping attempt (3): COCO_DVI_MODE=1 default = video_output_init(640,480) + set_dvi_mode(true) + native_pixel_mode + scanline POINTER callback, no compose ring. COCO_DVI_MODE=0 keeps the HDMI/precomposed path intact for FRUITJAM-14. REMAINDER, deliberately not held open here: (a) the ACR/audio-infoframe experiment -> FRUITJAM-14; (b) the core-0 timing step -> FRUITJAM-38; (c) README still describes the video path without the DVI-mode default -> FRUITJAM-20; (d) the one unexplained desync - accepted at 1-in-589 and self-recovering; file a new issue only if it recurs at a higher rate. [2026-08-26 the residual desync noted in item (d) DID recur at a higher rate -> split out as FRUITJAM-49 (high). It latches at boot roughly 1 in 4-5 and resync does not recover it.]

summary: Core-0 field time steps 13.2 -> 16.0 ms (1.26x -> 1.04x real-time) a couple of minutes after boot
description: Found while soak-testing FRUITJAM-37; NOT caused by it. Core 0 holds ~13.2 us/field (1.26x real-time) for roughly two minutes after boot, then makes a DISCRETE STEP to ~16.0 ms (1.04x real-time) and stays there, creeping down only slightly: 13092 -> 12052 (dip) -> 14699 -> 16077 -> 16053 -> 16043 ... over four consecutive reports. A step, not a drift. That takes headroom from ~23% to ~4%, which is uncomfortably close to losing real-time and is a plausible contributor to residual HSTX FIFO underruns. NOT the video path: the same steady-state ~16.0 ms appears across all three FRUITJAM-37 video configurations (HDMI+precomposed, DVI+classic copy, DVI+native pointer), which differ hugely in per-line ISR cost. Whatever it is, it is common to all of them. SUSPECTS, untested: (a) the emulated workload genuinely changes (something auto-runs, or BASIC leaves a startup path) - cycles/field are fixed at 14915 but the instruction mix is not; (b) the run loop starts including pace/idle time, note 16.0 ms is suspiciously near the 16762 us field period; (c) a thermal or clock event; (d) SD/FDC or USB host activity settling in. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PERF: docs/perf-log.md records '~23% headroom' and FRUITJAM-14's core-cost investigation reasons from '~12.9 ms of the 16.762 ms field'. If those were measured in the cold-start window, the documented headroom is optimistic and every decision resting on it - notably whether HSTX audio fits on core 0 - needs rechecking against the steady state. FIRST STEP: log a timestamp + the emulated PC/state at the step, and confirm whether it also occurs with the machine held at a bare Color BASIC prompt with no disk/cassette/AUTO.BIN. CAUTION 2026-08-26, per FRUITJAM-75: avg run is not a clean measure of core-0 work. Moving ONE function to RAM changed avg run by 1.5 ms with no behavioural change, and adding never-executed code changed it by the same amount. Any step in this figure must be checked against a layout-immune build before being attributed to load or to time-since-boot. RESOLVED 2026-08-27 by the FRUITJAM-75 long run: the step does NOT occur on time. A 3.3-hour idle capture (docs/logs/bisect-D-blitram.log, 3850 reports, 0 reboots) held avg run between 12383 and 13175 us for the entire run and never approached 16000. This issue claimed the step arrives 'a couple of minutes after boot' on ANY build; it did not arrive at all in 200 minutes. Meanwhile 16.0 ms was measured repeatedly and immediately whenever KALEIDSC was running, and 13.0-13.2 ms whenever the machine sat idle at the BASIC prompt - in BOTH the morning and evening sessions. CONCLUSION: the 13.2 -> 16.0 ms step is EMULATION LOAD (what the 6809 is executing changes the host cost of a fixed 14915-cycle budget, since opcodes differ in emulation cost), not time-since-boot. The original observation was almost certainly a program being started, not a timer firing. CAVEAT carried from FRUITJAM-75: avg run is also sensitive to code layout - moving one function to RAM shifted it by 1.5 ms - so any FUTURE step in this figure still needs checking against a layout-immune build before being attributed to load. CONSEQUENCE: perf-log.md's '~23% headroom' is no longer suspect on these grounds; idle really is ~1.27x real-time. Closing.
